description: My mission for the hackathon weekend is to design 'Kisaan Agriculture Intelligence': a platform helping regional farmers whose generational wisdom is failing due to unprecedented climate change. During the event, I plan to make an interactive decision-making platform that connects to NASA data portals and uses knowledge about multiple crops to help professionals adapt their farming practices to changing weather patterns.
summary:
Kisaan: Climate Resilient Agro Intelligence is an interactive geospatial climate simulator and crop decision-support platform designed to protect farmers whose generational knowledge and traditional wisdom are giving way due to rapid climate change. For decades, farming communities relied on inherited planting knowledge, but unpredictable heatwaves, sudden frost nights, and shifting soil moisture are making past patterns unreliable. Because smallholder farmers cannot afford to waste a single harvest, Kisaan bridges this gap by helping both older farmers and the new generation stay informed about recent environmental changes and adapt before planting.
Addressing the Field Shift challenge, Kisaan combines multi-year satellite telemetry from the NASA POWER Agroclimatology API with verified crop survival limits from the UN FAO EcoCrop Database. Users select any farming region, choose a crop and sowing date, and test historical extremes alongside a future temperature stress-test slider. If the selected crop faces high climate risk, the engine automatically recommends viable alternative crops with exact sowing-to-harvest dates.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:
Kisaan: Climate Resilient Agro Intelligence operates in two distinct states. On boot-up, users enter any farming region, which is geocoded via geopy (Nominatim) and plotted on an interactive native st.map() view backed by st.session_state so farmers can visually confirm their field coordinates. Once the user selects a crop, a planned sowing date, and a simulated temperature offset, the backend loops across three historical growing cycles (2025, 2024, 2023) using Python's datetime and timedelta modules. It sends live HTTP requests to the NASA POWER Agroclimatology API (community=ag) to retrieve daily records for surface soil heat (TS), 2-meter minimum frost temperature (T2M_MIN), and root-zone soil wetness (GWETPROF). The system extracts the worst historical drought, frost, and heat extremes, presents them in a Pandas summary table, and evaluates them against verified UN FAO EcoCrop survival limits. If the chosen crop fails any threshold, the substitution engine scans all baseline crops to recommend viable alternatives with exact sowing-to-harvest dates.

Benefits & Intended Impact:
In agricultural economies like Punjab, generational farming wisdom and inherited planting calendars are becoming unreliable due to climate volatility. Because smallholder farmers cannot afford to waste a single harvest, Kisaan bridges traditional agricultural knowledge with real space-agency telemetry—empowering both veteran farmers and the younger generation to stay informed about recent environmental shifts and make data-backed planting decisions before risking a season.

Tools, Languages & Engineering Choices:
The platform is hand-coded in Python using Streamlit, Pandas, Requests, and Geopy, and styled with a custom .streamlit/config.toml dark-space theme following Streamlit's official documentation. Key creative features and factors considered include:

  • Temperature Stress-Test Slider (-5.0°C to +5.0°C): Allows farmers to simulate future global warming spikes or sudden cold snaps rather than relying solely on historical averages.
  • Seasonal Duration Filtering: Ensures recommended replacement crops fit within the user's original seasonal growing window so planting calendars stay practical.
  • API Reliability & State Management: Uses custom geocoding timeouts (timeout=10) and st.session_state caching so the interface remains responsive and hides the map cleanly once simulation results render.

AI / Super Intelligence Disclosure:
All application architecture and code were hand-written by me. AI tools were used strictly as a reference assistant to look up library syntax, troubleshoot datetime and API debugging errors, and proofread written documentation. Presentation layout was drafted with AI assistance.
